Combine AKDE home ranges into population home ranges

Source: R/hr_tt_akde_pop.R
hr_tt_akde_pop.Rd

This function combines the utilisation distributions (UDs) of individual tracks estimated with hr_tt_akde() into population-level UDs, using the methods of the package ctmm. If x is grouped (e.g. by a variable of the metadata, such as sex or colony, joined to the table of UDs), a population UD is estimated for each group; otherwise, all the UDs are combined into a single population UD.

Usage

hr_tt_akde_pop(
  x,
  method = c("pkde", "mean"),
  tracks = NULL,
  models = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  sample = TRUE,
  levels = NULL,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  tolerance = 0.001,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A tibble of UDs estimated with hr_tt_akde() (with the ctmm UD objects in column ud_ctmm), possibly grouped (e.g. with dplyr::group_by()) to estimate a population UD for each group. Each group must contain at least two UDs (but see Details: groups of at least three are recommended).

method

The method used to combine the UDs, either "pkde" (the default) or "mean" (see Details).

tracks

The move2 object used to estimate the UDs with hr_tt_akde() (only needed with method = "pkde").

models

The table of models used to estimate the UDs, as created with ctmm_tt_fit() (only needed with method = "pkde").

weights

The weights of the individuals in the population UD. Either NULL (the default) for equal weights, or, with method = "mean", the name of a numeric column of x with the relative weight of each UD (non-negative, and not all zero within a group), or, with method = "pkde", TRUE to optimise the weights (see ctmm::pkde(); this requires the package quadprog). ctmm::pkde() cannot use weights given by the user.

sample

Logical; with method = "mean", whether the tracks are a sample of a larger population (TRUE, the default) or the whole population (FALSE).

levels

A vector of levels for the isopleths (i.e. contour lines), as numbers between 0 and 1. If NULL (the default), the full population UDs are returned; otherwise just the isopleths are returned, with the confidence intervals of their areas (as for hr_tt_akde()).

ci_level

The confidence level of the confidence intervals of the home range areas, returned when levels is set. Default is 0.95.

tolerance

With method = "pkde", the target error of the numerical computations of ctmm::pkde() (its error argument), which is also the largest probability mass of the population UD allowed outside the grid before the grid is extended. Default is 0.001.

...

Additional arguments passed to ctmm::pkde() (e.g. kernel).

Value

Either a tibble of class hr_tt_ud_tbl, or, if levels is not NULL, an sf tibble of class hr_tt_poly_tbl, with one row per group (and level), and columns:

  • the grouping variables of x (if x is grouped)

  • method: the method used to estimate the population UD ("pkde" or "akde_mean")

  • n_ud: the number of individual UDs combined

  • dof_area: the effective number of degrees of freedom of the population home range area

  • xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, res: the grid of the population UD (the grid of the individual UDs, possibly extended, see Details) If levels is NULL:

  • ud: the population UDs, as a list-column of terra::SpatRaster objects

  • ud_ctmm: the population UDs, as a list-column of ctmm UD objects Else, if levels is not NULL:

  • level, area, area_low, area_high and geometry, as returned by hr_tt_akde()

Details

Two methods are available:

  • "pkde" (the default): population kernel density estimation (ctmm::pkde()), which estimates the population UD from the locations of all the tracks of a group, using kernels based on the movement models of the individuals. This requires the tracks (tracks) and the models (models) used to estimate the individual UDs.

  • "mean": the (weighted) average of the individual UDs (ctmm::mean.UD()). The UD is the same as the one obtained with hr_tt_ud_sum(), but the ctmm UD object includes a population model, which is used to estimate the confidence intervals of the population home range area. With sample = TRUE (the default), the tracks are considered a sample of a larger population, and the uncertainty of the population distribution is taken into account.

In both cases, the uncertainty of the population home range areas reflects the variation among individuals, and it is large for groups with few individuals (as shown by small values of dof_area).

ctmm estimates some of the population-level parameters (e.g. the bandwidth of the population kernels with method = "pkde") with a stochastic optimiser, so the results can differ between runs. With method = "pkde", both the population UD and the confidence intervals of its area can differ; with method = "mean", the population UD is always the same, but the confidence intervals of its area (and dof_area) can differ. Set the seed of the random number generator (with set.seed()) before calling hr_tt_akde_pop() to get reproducible results.

Use groups of at least three individuals: with both methods, ctmm fits a population model to the movement models of the individuals, whose parameters are poorly determined with only two individuals, so that its optimiser can fail to converge and run for a very long time (depending on the seed). If a call runs for much longer than expected, add individuals to the group if possible, or try another seed.

Population kernel density estimation assumes that the individuals of a group are a sample from a single population, whose home ranges are distributed around a common centre (following a Gaussian distribution). Groups of individuals in distinct areas (e.g. different colonies) should be estimated separately (e.g. by grouping x by colony): pooling them leads to a very smooth population UD, which can miss the areas used by a minority of individuals.

All the UDs of a group must be estimated on the same grid (as is the case for the UDs returned by a single call of hr_tt_akde() without a bbox for each group), and the population UD is estimated on that grid. With method = "pkde", the kernels of the population are wider than those of the individuals, so the population UD can extend beyond the grid of the individual UDs; in this case, the grid is extended (by whole cells, so that it stays aligned with the original grid, and in the same way for all groups that shared it) to contain the population UD.

See also

hr_tt_akde() to estimate the individual UDs, hr_tt_ud_sum() to combine UDs from any method (without confidence intervals).

Examples

data(buffalo, package = "ctmm")
buffalo_tt <- mt_as_move2(buffalo)
# we use a subset of three buffalo to make the example fast
buffalo_sub <- buffalo_tt %>%
  filter_by_meta(track %in% c("Cilla", "Gabs", "Mvubu")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(track) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 100) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
# fitting the models and estimating the UDs take several seconds
# \donttest{
buffalo_fit <- ctmm_tt_fit(buffalo_sub, model = "ou")
#> Minimum sampling interval of 59 minutes in Cilla
#> Minimum sampling interval of 57 minutes in Gabs
#> Minimum sampling interval of 59 minutes in Mvubu
buffalo_akde <- hr_tt_akde(buffalo_sub, buffalo_fit)
# population UD with population kernel density estimation (setting the seed
# for reproducible results, see Details)
set.seed(1)
buffalo_pop <- hr_tt_akde_pop(
  buffalo_akde,
  tracks = buffalo_sub,
  models = buffalo_fit
)
buffalo_pop
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   method  n_ud dof_area   xmin    ymin   xmax   ymax   res ud                
#>   <chr>  <int>    <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <named list>      
#> 1 pkde       3     7.48 22353. -12467. 55201. 14023.  118. <SpatRstr[,279,1]>
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: ud_ctmm <named list>
# or as the average of the individual UDs, with the 95% home range
set.seed(1)
hr_tt_akde_pop(buffalo_akde, method = "mean", levels = 0.95)
